entries.name: Dead tree
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours, bare branching trunk (Quaternius 2019)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: The plan's source (a Quaternius dead tree on poly.pizza) is behind a Cloudflare challenge; this is CommonTree_Dead_1 from Quaternius's Ultimate Nature Pack on OpenGameArt (License.txt in the zip: CC0 1.0), the same zip as the tree, tree-pine, tree-autumn, tree-palm and bush entries, so they read as one set. Of the fifteen bare trees in the pack (CommonTree_Dead_1-5, BirchTree_Dead_1-5, Willow_Dead_1-5; the Snow variants left out) it has the clearest dead-tree silhouette: one trunk forking at 2.5 m into two wide limbs that each split into a fan of crooked twigs, 6.7 m across, the classic bare tree against a winter or Halloween sky. CommonTree_Dead_3/4 are thin poles with three or four prongs, _2/_5 bunch their branches into a narrow crown, the Willow_Dead trunks lean hard and have few, thick, antler-like branches, and the BirchTree_Dead bark is white (birch is already the tree-autumn entry, and pale bark washes out on a pale sky). Yaw 90 puts the broad side of the fork (6.7 m wide, 3.3 m deep) to the front. Height 7 m: the same size as the broadleaf tree, a dead oak or maple in a field, graveyard or winter park is 6-9 m; the fork sits at about 2.5 m, above a 1.6 m person. Colours on noon: bark iris shading to ink, a dark warm brown that reads hard against the pale paper sky and between the near-black broadleaf trunk and the pale palm trunk. Static: no clips.
